*श्री देवजी एम. पटेल (जालौर)ः खाद और यूरिया एक ऐसी चीज़ है, जो किसानों को समय पर नहीं मिली तो खेती खराब हो जाती है, खेती के लिए यूरिया सही समय पर सही मात्रा में मिलना जरूरी है। भारत को यूरिया अधिक मात्रा में आयात करना पड़ता है। देश में उत्पादन कम होता है। एक अनुमान के अनुसार देश में 15 से 20 लाख टन यूरिया प्रत्येक फसल के समय विदेश से आयात करना पड़ता है। समय पर आयात नहीं करने से यूरिया समय पर खेत तक नहीं पहुंच पाता है। इसलिए मेरा आग्रह है कि समय से पूर्व ही यूरिया का आयात कर लिया जाए। आज आवश्यकता इस बात की है कि देश के सभी जिला केंद्रों पर यूरिया का स्टोरेज सरकार के द्वारा किया जाए। जिससे आयात करने व खेत तक यूरिया को समय पर पहुंचाया जा सके। आज राजस्थान सरकार की तारीफ करनी चाहिए, क्योंकि राजस्थान सरकार इस बजट में प्रत्येक जिला केंद्र पर स्टोरेज की सुविधा देने जा रही है।

यह देश का दुर्भाग्य है कि 2014 में यूरिया उत्पादन करने वाली चार बड़ी इकाईयां बंद हो गयी हैं। देश में पिछले एक देशक में एक भी यूरिया का कारखाना नहीं लगा। वहीं 1990 से अब तक यूरिया उत्पादन करने वाले 13 संयंत्र बंद पड़े हैं। यू.पी.ए. सरकार ने एक के बाद एक कारखाने बंद होने दिए और उनके कुछ गलत निर्देशों के कारण देश मे यूरिया का संकट गहराता गया। अतः आज आवश्यकता है नये कारखाने लगाए जाए और आयात पर निर्भरता को कम किया जाए। राजस्थान स्थित जालौर-सिरोही में जमीन और संसाधानों की उपलब्धता को देखते हुए यहां यूरिया का बड़ा कारखाना लगाया जा सकता है। जालौर से कांडला बंदरगाह से करीब होने तथा रेलवे का आधारभूत संरचना होने से यह इलाका सर्वदा अनुकूल है।

एक तरफ देश मे यूरिया का उत्पादन कम होता है, हम आयात पर निर्भर रहते हैं, वहीं दूसरी तरफ बेहद लचर वितरण प्रणाली और कालाबाज़ारी इस कमी को उस मुकाम पर ले जाती है, जहां किसान या तो कराह उठता है या फिर हल की जगह खेती-बाड़ी को छोड़कर सड़क जाम और पुलिस की लाठियों से संघर्ष करता रहता है। रातों की नींद की छोड़कर एक कट्टे यूरिया के लिए कभी दुकान पर तो कभी थाने के बाहर लाइन में खड़ा रहता है। आज किसानों की सबसे बड़ी जरूरत यूरिया है। हमे यूरिया पर किसानों का सीधे सब्सिडी देनी चाहिए। किसान बाज़ार मूल्य पर यूरिया खरीदे और सब्सिडी की रकम उनके खाते में सीधे पहॅंच जाए। यह पहल यूरिया की कालाबाज़ारी रोकने में मददगार होगी, क्योंकि निजी दुकानों पर छापे और यूरिया की बोरियां जब्त होने की घटनाएं यहीं से जुड़ी है। इस तरह की शिकायतें बड़े पैमाने पर आ रही है कि सहकारी समिति में खाद उपलब्ध नहीं होती, लेकिन निजी दुकानों पर ऊंचे दाम पर यूरिया मिल रही है। उधर यूरिया खाद के अधिकृत विक्रेता कट्टे के साथ जबरन 200 रूपए की घटिया कीटनाशक किसानों को खरीदेने पर मजबूर करते हैं और बंदरगाहों से यूरिया पोटाश की अंतर्राष्ट्रीय तस्करी भी बड़ी समस्या बनती जा रही है। इस समस्या के अलावा राज्य सरकारों की लचर वितरण प्रणाली भी किसानों की दुश्मन बनी है।

हमारी सरकार यूरिया की समस्या के दूसरे पहलू पर विचार कर रही है। सरकार नें किसानों के लिए मिट्टी की जांच की सुविधा सुलभ कर दी है। हाल ही में प्रधानमंत्री महोदय ने सॉयल हैल्थ कार्ड योजना भी लागू की है, जिससे किसानों को अपने खेत की मिट्टी की सेहत व पोषक तत्वों की जरूरत की जानकारी होगी। इसके साथ ही किसानों को उर्वरकों के उपयोग की वैज्ञानिक सिफारिश भी प्राप्त होगी। किसानों से अपेक्षा की जाती है कि वे सभी उर्वरकों का संतुलित उपयोग करके अधिक पैदावार तथा अधिक लाभ अर्जित करें। जहां तक यूरिया के उपयोग की बात है, वैज्ञानिकों ने पत्तियों के रंग के आधार पर फसल की नाइट्रोजन आवश्यकता को आंकने की तकनीकी विकसित की है। इसे लीफ कलर चार्ट या एल.सी.सी. कहते हैं। सभी मुख्य फसलों में खासतौर से चावल और गेहूं मे एल.सी.सी. तकनीक के आधार पर यूरिया का उपयोग करने का बढ़ावा देना चाहिए। इससे यूरिया का कम और कुशल उपयोग सुनिश्चित होता है। यह एक बहुत ही सार्थक कदम है।

दूसरा महत्वपूर्ण निर्णय हमारी सरकार ने लिया है नीम कोटेड यूरिया का उत्पादन देश में बड़ी मात्रा में करने का है। जिससे किसानों को यूरिया की समस्या सब्सिडी आदि से निजात मिल जाए। नीम कोटेड यूरिया नीम के तेल से तैयार की जाती है। इसकी कीमत आम यूरिया की तुलना में 5 फीसदी ज्यादा होती है। इससे यूरिया उत्पादक कंपनिया नीम कोटेड यूरिया तैयार करने पर आने वाली अतिरिव्त लागत निकालती है। नीम कोटेड यूरिया सामान्य यूरिया की तुलना में ज्यादा प्रभावी भी होती है। केंद्र सरकार ने देश में नीम कोटेड यूरिया के इस्तेमाल को बढ़ावा देने का फैसला किया है। इसके लिए उर्वरक विभाग यूरिया का उत्पादन करने वाली कंपनियों को कुल उत्पादन का 50 फीसदी तक नीम कोटेड यूरिया का उत्पादन करने की अनुमति दे सकती है। नीम कोटेड यूरिया सामान्य यूरिया की तुलना में ज्यादा प्रभावी होती है। सरकार धीरे-धीरे नीम कोटेड यूरिया उत्पादन करने की सीमा बढ़ाकर 100 फीसदी तक करने पर भी विचार कर रहा है। नीम कोटेड यूरिया में मौजूद नाइट्रोजन धीरे-धीरे रिलीज होती है। इससे उर्वरक वेस्ट नहीं होता है। सरकार का यह फैसला उर्वरक उद्योग और किसानों दोनों ही के लिए लाभदायक है। इससे पहले कंपनियों को अपने कारखाने की कुल उत्पादन क्षमता के महत 35 फीसदी तक ही नीम कोटेड यूरिया बनाने की अनुमति थी।

मुझे पूरी तरह से विश्वास है कि आने वाले दिनों में जिला केन्द्र पर भण्डारण और नीम कोटेड यूरिया के निर्माण से किसानों को कालाबाज़ारी, यूरिया की कमी से मुव्ति मिल जाएगी।

SHRI ANANDRAO ADSUL (AMRAVATI): Hon. Chairperson, I rise to speak on the Demands for Grants of the Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers. The contribution of agriculture accounts for one-seventh of the GDP. The agricultural production in the year 1951-52 was 52 million metric tonnes and in the year 2013-14 it was 264.7 million metric tonnes which is about five times more. This is because of the significant role played by chemicals and fertilizers which is well recognized.

Today our country has achieved 80 per cent self-sufficiency in the production capacity of urea. As a result, India could substantially manage its requirement in nitrogenous fertilizers. We have also developed 50 per cent indigenous capacity in respect of phosphatic fertilizers. The installed capacity has reached a level of 132.58 lakh metric tonnes of nitrogen and 70.60 lakh metric tonnes of phosphatic nutrient in the year 2014-15, making India the third largest fertilizer producer in the world.

There are 30 urea production units in the country. The current demand for urea is around 31.8 million metric tonnes. Our indigenous production is about 28 million metric tonnes and the shortfall is met through import. Due to shortage of domestic gas, many naphtha based urea plants have converted to gas.

I would like to impress upon the Minister that the new policy of the Government to decontrol the movement of fertilizers may include fertilizer companies to supply fertilizers only to those areas which are more profitable and accessible as compared to those areas which are less profitable and inaccessible. So, the hon. Minister should have a rethinking on this policy. I would like to suggest that the Department of Fertilizers should build an institutional mechanism to monitor the movement of fertilizers.

Sir, the drastic reduction in the allocation of Plan funds clearly shows the Department’s poor budgetary planning and its unrealistic estimation of funds. The Department has rolled over the arrears of unpaid subsidy of Rs. 40,340.78 crore to the next year. The Department was allocated an amount of Rs. 74,092.73 crore against the requirement of Rs. 1,56,420.48 crore which is less than 50 per cent of the demand.

There are five closed units of Fertilizers Corporation of India in Sindhri, Talcher, Ramagundam, Gorakhpur and Korba and one closed unit of Hindustan Fertilizer Corporation at Barauni. Besides this, there are three sick units namely Madras Fertilizers Limited, Brahmaputra Valley Fertilizers Corporation of India Limited and Fertilizers and Chemicals Travancore Limited (FACT). I would like to urge upon the Minister that he should seriously look into the matter of closed units and take efforts to revive them so that we can meet our requirement for fertilizers only through indigenous production. This is very important.

Now I come to the field of chemicals and petrochemicals. The production of chemicals and petrochemicals was 10,328 thousand metric tonnes. It has declined by 0.7 per cent in 2014-15 as compared to previous year which was 10,402 thousand metric tonnes. Secondly, Indian chemicals sector spends only 1.2 per cent on research and development as against developed countries which are spending 5 to 10 per cent of their total turnover.

Import of chemicals contributed 9.9 per cent of the total import in 2013-14, whereas export contributed 9.3 per cent in the total export in 2014-15 as compared to 9.2 per cent in 2013-14. Concerted and coordinated efforts may be made to develop roadmap for indigenous development of the chemical sector in the country and also to expedite the process to set up reserve SEZ. In case of export to European countries, there is a problem in meeting the standards because of legislation for import of chemical from other countries. European Union’s registration, evaluation, authorization and restrictions of chemical standards are very strict.

I want to point out that the administration in chemicals and petrochemicals is very disjointed as the Department of Chemicals and Petrochemicals of the Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers does not deal with all the chemical and petrochemical items. This is most important. As an illustration, agro-chemicals are with the Ministry of Agriculture; soaps and detergents are with the DIPP. Out of four units, the petrochemical units are under the control of the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas. So, all these units should be brought under the Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers.

Now I come to pharmaceuticals. Budgetary support to the Department of Pharmaceuticals is Rs. 210 crore for plan and 47.02 crore for non-plan. It is very painful to say that the country has spent Rs. 17,944.05 crore to import medicinal and pharmaceutical products. Instead of this, if the Government would have revived the closed and sick public sector units, it would expedite enhancing the current capacity of the bulk drugs in the country itself and making the country self-reliant in bulk drugs.

The outlay of Rs. 12,341.89 crore was proposed by the Department for the 12th Five Year Plan covering various schemes to the Planning Commission against which an allocation of Rs. 2,968 crore was approved. Funds allocated to the Department, the Ministry of Finance are low with reference to their proposals. In the absence of adequate funds, the schemes and programmes undertaken would be adversely affected.

I now come to the Jan Aushadhi Yojana which is unique and very much beneficial to the common man of the country. This scheme was launched by the UPA Government in 2008 which had decided to open at least 630 Jan Aushadhi shops in each district of the country. But, unfortunately, only 170 shops were opened. Nowadays, out of them, 98 shops are running. My request to the Minister is this. Jan Aushadhi is very much useful for the common man. In comparison of the branded drugs, it is four to sixteen times cheaper than the branded drugs. That is why, re-launching of this scheme is very much essential. I would suggest that in each and every district, at block level, we should open Jan Aushadhi shops. If we open the Jan Aushadhi shops, the common man will easily get them at low cost. Nowadays, you see there are so many diseases and costly medicines are required for their treatment. That is why my request to the Minister is, you please look into the matter seriously and re-launch this scheme and open the Jan Aushadhi shops at the block level. Thank you.

SHRI THOTA NARASIMHAM (KAKINADA): Chairman, Sir, I am thankful to you for giving me an opportunity to speak a few words on an important subject like Chemical Fertilizers. Agricultural productivity depends on various factors like soil fertility, climatic conditions, irrigation facilities, seed quality etc., but more importantly on usage of optimum primary, secondary and micro nutrients. Being the backbone of agricultural productivity, the role of fertilizers will always remain crucial. India has emerged as the third largest producer of nitrogenous fertilizers.

Chemical fertilizers have been playing an important role in making the country self-reliant in food grain production. The policies of the Government have to be conducive to increase the availability and consumption of fertilizers at affordable prices and at an appropriate time in the country.

Due to over usage of pesticides, pests are developing resistance. It also leads to bioaccumulation of dangerous chemical components in the higher stages of food chain and causing severe health consequences. Moreover, excessive usage of fertilizers is the main reason for ground water pollution.

Since 1991, the Government has made several attempts to rationalize fertilizer subsidy to address fiscal deficit and distributional and environmental concerns. There is every need to bring about greater efficiency in the production of fertilizers; reduce expenditure on fertilizer subsidy; and also bring about regional and nutritional balance in the usage of fertilizers.

Regarding fertilizer subsidy, it is necessary to examine both the demand and supply side of the fertilizer sector. At the time of Green Revolution, the Government of India encouraged farmers to use fertilizers to increase the production in the name of self-sufficiency and food security, having not in mind its adverse impact in future. Reports reveal that agricultural growth rate is satisfactory. But unfortunately, it is due to the increase in cultivable land and not owing to the increase in per hectare productivity. Rather, it is depleting. The subsidies on fertilizers, introduced by the successive Governments, have even made it worse. The illiterate farmers, not knowing the disastrous impact of chemical fertilizers, simply concentrated on the quantity rather than quality. Due to the indiscriminate usage of fertilizers, the fertility of the soil had gone down and affected the agricultural production. In fact, there are limitations to increase the marginal productivity of crop by marginal increase in application of fertilizers. It is zero after a certain extent. Further, the nature of soils in India is complexed and diversified. Now, it is the time to set things right by encouraging research and development in agricultural sciences by providing better facilities in Agricultural Universities to innovate and adopt modern agricultural techniques best suited to our system rather than simply copying the foreign methods. It is also important to revive the traditional farming techniques like water conservation methods followed in Rajasthan and leaving straw on fields after yield for nutrient percolation into soil as followed by some farmers in Kerala etc. That will make our agriculture sustainable. It will also ensure food security and health to all our citizens. Otherwise, future generations will curse us. 

I congratulate the Government for initiating farmer friendly schemes like Soil Health Cards, Kisan Call Centre, Kisan Television, Mobile Soil Testing Centres etc. Kisan Call Centres are giving information to the farmers regarding usage of chemical fertilizers and pesticides but they are not providing any information with regard to organic farming techniques and application of bio manures. I heard that there are plenty of enquiries coming from farmers requesting for organic farming techniques and use of bio manures. My suggestion is to include the same in the Kisan Call Centre for the benefit of the farming community. 

The fertilizer subsidy regime has contributed to an unbalanced use of nutrients with possible negative consequences for soil health and productivity. 

The primary threat is that of nutrient mining: crops draw nutrients from the soil far in excess of those applied in the form of fertilizers. Indian soils are losing not only nitrogen, phosphorous and potassium but also crucial micronutrients such as sulphur, zinc, iron and boron. While the ratio of NPK and fertilizer use was never close to the ideal position in India, it has faced substantial distortion during the past decade and a half.

HON. CHAIRPERSON : Please conclude now.

SHRI THOTA NARASIMHAM: Sir, I will take one more minute.

Nowadays organic farming products have attained great demand. People are purchasing organic products even though they are a little bit costly. I personally feel that it is time for the Government to take steps to encourage our traditional organic farming in a big way.

Sir, in my constituency, Kakinada, there are fertilizer companies like Nagarjuna Fertilisers, Coromondal Fertilisers, Godavari Fertilisers. Nagarjuna Fertilisers and Chemicals Limited is the gas-based urea manufacturing plant located in Kakinada. Due to recent gas blow-out at Nagaram, East Godavari, Andhra Pradesh, there is a dearth of gas supply to NFCL, which has an adverse effect on its production. It can produce 16 lakh tonnes of urea but it has produced nine lakh tonnes only during 2014-15. Even though NFCL is capable of taking 3.2 million cubic metres of gas per day, it is getting only 2.5 million cubic metres per day. I would request the Government to restore the normalcy in the gas supply at the earliest in the interest of the farming community. Sir, a few years back, at that time as the Minister of Chemicals and Fertilisers, Shri Ananthkumar visited Kakinada and inspected that plant also.

Thank you very much.

*श्रीमती अंजू बाला (मिश्रिख)ः मुझे आज "रसायन और उर्वरक" पर चर्चा में मैं बताना चाहती हॅं। जब किसान खेती करता है तो उसे सबसे पहली जरूरत "खाद" की ही होती है। जिसके बिना हमारे "अन्नदाता" जो हमारा किसान है, जो अन्न उगाता है, जो रात-दिन नहीं देखता है, धूप-छॉव नहीं देखता है और हमारे लिए अनाज उगाता है, उसे सबसे पहले "खाद" की आवश्यकता होती है। जिसके लिए उसे हमेशा संघर्ष करना पड़ता है।

इस सरकार की तरफ से "उर्वरक" जाता है किसानों के पास, परंतु कभी समय पर पहुंचा हो, ऐसा अभी तक नहीं हुआ। होता तो यह है कि प्रत्येक फसल मौसम के आरंभ होने से पूर्व राज्य सरकारों के परामर्श से कृषि एवं सहकारिता विभाग द्वारा माह-वार मांग का आंकलन तथा निरूपण किया जाता है। माह-वार एवं राज्यवार अनुमान के आधार पर उर्वरक विभाग मासिक आपूर्ति योजना जारी करके राज्यों को पर्याप्त मात्रा में उर्वरकों का आवंटन करता है तथा एक ऑनलाइन वेब आधारित निगरानी प्रणाली जिसे उर्वरक निगरानी प्रणाली कहा जाता है, द्वारा देशभर में राजसहायता वाले सभी प्रमुख उर्वरकों की आवाजाही की निगरानी की जाती है। राज्य सरकारों को अपनी राज्य संस्थानिक एजेंसियों जैसे मार्कफेड आदि के माध्यम से रेलवे रैक के लिए समय पर इंडेंट देकर आपूर्तियों को कारगर बनाने के लिए उर्वरकों को विनिर्माताओं एवं आयातकों के साथ समन्वय स्थापित करने के लिए नियमित रूप से सलाह दी जाती है। कृषि एवं सहकारिता विभाग, उर्वरक विभाग तथा रेल मंत्रालय द्वारा राज्य कृषि अधिकारियों के साथ संयुव्त रूप से नियमित साप्ताहिक वीडियो कांप्रंॊEस का आयोजन किया जाता है तथा राज्य सरकारों द्वारा इंगित किया गया था कि उर्वरक प्रेषित करने के लिए सुधारात्मक कदम उठाये जाते हैं। मांग तथा उत्पादन के बीच अंतर को आयात के माध्यम से पूरा किया जाता है। इसके अलावा उर्वरकों को आवश्यक वस्तु अधिनियम, 1955 के तहत आवश्यक वस्तु के रूप में घोषित किया गया है। किसानों को तर्कसंगत कीमत पर उर्वरकों की पर्याप्त उपलब्धता सुनिश्चित करने के उद्देश्य से भारत सरकार ने आवश्यक वस्तु अधिनियम की धारा-3 के तहत उर्वरक नियंत्रण आदेश (एस.सी.ओ.)-1985 प्रतिपादित किया गया है। एफ.सी.ओ. राज्य सरकारों को तर्कसंगत कीमत पर अपने-अपने राज्यों को उर्वरक उपलबध कराने के लिए उपयुव्त कदम उठाने की शव्ति प्रदान करता है। उर्वरक विभाग राज्य स्तर तक सभी उर्वरकों की उपलब्धता सुनिश्चित करता है तथा राज्यों के अंदर उर्वरक के वितरण की जिम्मेदारी राज्य सरकारों की होती है। लगभग सभी राज्य सरकारें ब्लॉक स्तरीय अनुमान एवं आपूर्ति योजना तैयार करती हैं, परंतु वे जिला स्तर तक ही निगरानी करती हैं। उपर्युव्त स्थिति के बावजूद भी तथ्य यह है कि बुवाई के समय भी किसानों को आवश्यकतानुसार उर्वरकों की आपूर्ति नहीं की जाती है। मेरा यह मानना है कि आवश्यकता/उपलब्धता/बिक्री से संबंधित आंकड़ें वास्तविकता से बिल्कुल परे हैं। हम यह महसूस करते हैं कि विभाग इस मामले में सर्वथा अपनी जिम्मेदारी से नहीं बच सकता है। जिस प्रकार की प्रौद्योगिकी आज उपलब्ध है उसके द्वारा अंतिम प्रयोव्ता अर्थात् किसान तक पहुंचने तक उर्वरक की आवाजाही की निगरानी करना व्यवहार्य होगा। उर्वरक की कोई कमी होने पर विभाग द्वारा तत्काल सुधारात्मक उपाए किये जाने चाहिए। इसीलिए यह होना चाहिए कि देश के किसी हिस्से में स्थानीय स्तर पर भी उर्वरकों की किसी कमी से निपटने के लिए राज्य सरकारों के समन्वय से उव्ररकों की आवाजाही की निगरानी हेतु प्रणाली को और ज्यादा प्रभावशाली बनाया जाए। जो उर्वरक बिक्री केंद्र उर्वरक की दुकानों के रूप में राज्यों में कृषि विभाग की निगरानी में खोले जाते हैं तथा कृषि विभाग द्वारा उर्वरक बिक्री के लिए जो लाइसेंस जारी किए जाते हैं, उनका सरकारी शुल्क बहुत ही कम होता है, परंतु लाइसेंस जारी करने वाले अधिकारी लाइसेंस लेने वाले व्यव्ति से रिश्वत के रूप में मोटी रकम वसूल करते हैं। जिसके कारण लाइसेंस धारक पहले दिन से ही उर्वरक की कालाबाज़ारी शुरू कर देता है। इस व्यवस्था में परिवर्तन की आवश्यकता है। उर्वरक की कालाबाज़ारी रोकने के लिए तथा किसानों को खाद बाज़ार मूल्य पर मिल सके, इसके लिए आवश्यकता है कि सरकार द्वारा उर्वरक पर दी जाने वाली सब्सिडी उर्वरक कारखानों के बजाए सीधे किसानों को दी जाए।

ऒडॉ. सुनील बलीराम गायकवाड़ (लातूर): भारत सरकार के केमिकल एंड फर्टिलाइजर मंत्रालय के माध्यम से देश में सभी कृषि क्षेत्र के लिए खल (यूरिया) जैसे बहुत ही महत्वपूर्ण खल की सफाई अच्छी तरह से होना चाहिए । अगर उत्पादन है तो उसका मार्केटिंग या बाजार में किसानों को सहज उपलब्ध किया जाए । मेरे निर्वाचन क्षेत्र लातूर महाराष्ट्र में खेतों के सारीचार्ज हुआ था । सरकार सभी किसानों को उपलब्ध मुख्यक मात्रा में करना चाहिए । एक तो निर्सग किसानों को साथ नही देना, बारीस अच्छी मात्रा में नहीं होती है । अच्छी फसल उगाने के लिए खेतों की जरूरत सरकार की तरफ से पूरी तरह पूरी नहीं की जाती है । परिणाम यह निसर्ग की भी साथ नहीं मिलती है । ऐसे हाल में भारत सरकार ने मुख्यक समाज में किसानों के हित में फर्टिलाइजर के लिए राष्ट्रीय केमिकल एंड फर्टिलाइजर आरसीएफ से मुंबई में स्थित कंपनी का उत्पादन क्षमता बढ़ाने की जरूरत है ।

देश के कोने-कोने में आरसीएफ की एजेंसीज देनी चाहिए अभी जो है । उसके अतिरिक्त भी नई एजेंसीज देने की जरूरत है । केमिकल एंड फर्टिलाइर मंत्रालय का देश के लिए महत्वपूर्ण योगदान है ।

मैं सरकार से अनुरोध करता हूं कि देश के किसानों और जनता का हित ध्यान में लेकर ज्यादा से ज्यादा किसानों को लाभ मिले ।

सरकार की कुछ केमिकल कंपनी जो बंद पड़ी हुई है । उसे पुनः शुरू करने का प्रयास अगर करते हैं तो देश के लोगों को इससे फायदा हो सकता है ।

एग्रो केमिकल, पेट्रोकेमिकल जैसे अलग-अलग टाईप के केमिकल्स हो उसके उद्योग के लिए भी बढ़ावा देना चाहिए ।

* Speech was laid on the Table

*श्री बोध सिंह भगत (बालाघाट)ः मैं रसायन व उर्वरक मंत्रालय की बजट अनुदान मांगों का समर्थन करता हॅं तथा कटौती प्रस्ताव का विरोध करता हॅं। हमारा देश एक कृषि प्रधान देश है। भारत सरकार देश में रासायनिक उर्वरकों की खपत तथा उपलब्धता को बढ़ाने तथा उसके द्वारा देश में अधिकतम कृषि उत्पादन हेतु अनुकूल नीतियों का अनुसरण कर रही है। इस उद्देश्य की प्राप्ति के लिए सरकार उर्वरक क्षेत्र में उद्योगों को बढ़ावा दे रही है। मध्य प्रदेश के अधिकांश लोगों के साथ-साथ मेरे लोक सभा क्षेत्र बालाघाट, सिवनी के अधिकतम लोगों का मुख्य रोज़गार खेती है। खेती में उर्वरक व कीटनाशकों का बहुत महत्व है। समय पर इनकी उपलब्धता तथा प्रयोग का सीधा प्रभाव फसल की उपज पर पड़ता है। खाद व कीटनाशक रसायनों की बढ़ती कीमत से जहां एक तरफ कृषि लागत बढ़ी है, वहीं दूसरी ओर समय पर उपलब्धता न होने के कारण इसका सीधा प्रभाव उत्पादन व किसान की आमदनी पर पड़ता है। उर्वरक तस्करी रोकने से सीधे किसानों को लाभ पहुंचाने हेतु उर्वरकों पर दी जा रही सब्सिडी को सीधे कृषकों के बैंक खाते में डालना जाए। बालाघाट-सिवनी मेरा संसदीय क्षेत्र कृषि प्रधान है। जिसमें समय पर खाद उपलब्ध न होने के कारण उत्पादन प्रभावित होता है। वर्तमान में रेक प्वाइंट गोंधिया महाराष्ट्र है, जिसके कारण परिवहन में परेशानी होती है। अतः रेक प्वाइंट बालाघाट किया जाये, जिससे किसानों को सुलभता से खाद उपलब्ध हो सके।

केंद्रीय रसायन एव उर्वरक मंत्री जी द्वारा फार्माजन समाधान योजना लांच की है। इस योजना से दवाओं की कीमतों एवं उपलब्धता के बारे में ग्राहकों की शिकायतों के निवारण की वेब आधारित प्रणाली है। लोगों को दवाओं की गैर वाजिब कीमतों, दवाओं की गैर उपलबधता अथवा किल्लत,एन.पी.पी.ए. की मूल्य संबंधी स्वीकृति के बगैर ही नई दवाओं की बिक्री और किसी समुचित कारण के बगैर ही किसी दवा की बिक्री के लिए आपूर्ति से इंकार करने से जुड़ी अपनी शिकायतों के निवारण के लिए ऑनलाइन सुविधा मिलेगी। एन.पी.पी.ए. कोई भी शिकायत मिलने के 48 घंटे के अंदर कार्यवाही शुरू कर देगा, जिससे कृषकों का शोषण रूकेगा।

अतः मैं पुनः अनुदान मांगों का समर्थन व कटौती प्रस्ताव का विरोध करता हॅं।

SHRI KOTHA PRABHAKAR REDDY (MEDAK): Sir, Hyderabad provides 33 per cent of the bulk drugs required for the nation. The bulk drug industries are growing at the rate of nine per cent per year. The related issues are to be addressed effectively in a time bound frame for economic growth. The bulk drug industries are classified under Red Zone by the Ministry of Environment and Forests due to its hazardous nature while processing and disposal of wastes. Though efficient treatment plants and solid waste management plants using the latest technology have been available for disposal of wastes in a scientific manner, the same is not being implemented due to lack of will, vision and resources.

One of our NGOs (Save our Urban Lakes) found that lakes in and around Hyderabad and Medak districts, Jinnaram Mandal, Khazipalli and Jillelavagu lakes have the highest industrial pollutants. The pharmaceutical industries are pumping chemical wastes from their units through bore wells into the ground, spoiling and polluting the lake water and groundwater. These polluted lakes are filled with bacteria that are resistant to wide range of antibiotics. This is causing people around these lakes to be immune to a wide range of antibiotics. 

In view of these problems, the Government of India should regulate and monitor the norms for waste treatment management to safeguard the interests of the people and make sure that these industries practice zero discharge effluents. It is my considered suggestion. 

The requirement of by-products of petrochemicals like polymers and polypropane for manufacturing of injection moulds, cement bags, milk and oil pouches and Tupperware products in Telangana is estimated at 20,000 metric tonnes per month. 

Most of the requirements are met by transporting the raw materials in the form of solid and liquid from other States. So, is there any proposal to develop the petrochemical complex to support the industries in the newly formed Telangana State? It would be very much useful for the plastic park.

Sir, I would request the Government to speed up the revival process of Ramagundam Fertilisers and Chemicals Limited to produce gas-based ammonia and urea (ammonia – 3854 metric tonnes per day, urea – 2200 metric tonnes per day) and commence production on or before 2018 with composition of fertilisers to sustain the agricultural products against industrial pollutants and to promote the farming sector, employment and economic growth of the Region. 

With these words, I conclude. Thank you.

* SHRI S.R. VIJAYA KUMAR (CHENNAI CENTRAL) : I thank our revered hon. Makkalin Mudalvar Idhayan Deivam Puratchi Thalaivi Dr. Amma for having given me an opportunity to represent Central Chennai Lok Sabha Constituency and also for enabling me to participate in the discussion on the Demands for Grants for the Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers for the year 2015-16.

This Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers consists of three Departments of the Ministry, viz. the Department of Chemicals and Petrochemicals, the Department of Fertilizers and the Department of Pharmaceuticals.

Let me submit my views department-wise.

The Budget Estimates for the Department of Chemicals and Petrochemicals is put at Rs.255.18 crores out of which Rs.188 crores for Plan outlay and Rs.67.18 crores for non-Plan outlay. The total Budget Estimates for this Department is almost only 25 percent of total Actuals of Rs.1208.58 crores for the year 2013-14. The vast reduction in the Budget allocation from the Actuals of the year 2013-14 done in the fiscal 2014-15 by the previous Government is being followed by this Government in the present fiscal 2015-16 also. In the Chemicals sector, there is scope for development of new and commercially producible and easily usable, bio-degradable and environment-friendly organic products by the Government owned PSUs like Hindustan Organic Chemicals Limited (HOCL). But we don't understand why there is no new investment in this area. It is sad that we as a big nation do not invest in environment-friendly technologies and produce indigenous products for our people in general and for our farmers in particular. The year after year consistent reduction in Plan outlay for this Department is happening at a time when importance of this chemicals and petrochemicals is felt worldwide. Petrochemicals industries are also vital because of their vast potential for wide use of the Petrochemical products and also the huge employment opportunities that can be created by the industry. Petrochemicals sector should not be completely left at the mercy of the private players without any new Government investment in this sector. I hope the Government will relook into this issue and come out with reasonable allocation.

Coming to the Department of Fertilizers, the Budget Estimates for this Department is put at Rs.73,047.90 crores out of which Rs.50 crores for Plan outlay and Rs.72,997.80 crores for non-Plan outlay. The total Budget Estimates for this Department shows no major increase despite our Government's policy to help our farmers to produce more.

The huge non-Plan outlay for this Department is to meet the fertilizer subsidy. Almost same allocation like the previous year's figures means there is no substantial increased benefit proposed to be given to the poor farmers of this country. Nobody will question the necessity to subsidize the cost of fertilizers which is a major component in the farm input cost. Our poor farmers are suffering due to various ills like economically unviable small land holdings, absence of well-planned and well-executed agricultural financing, unpredictable monsoon, lack of availability of latest irrigation and farm technologies, absence of localized and area-specific farm technique teaching by the Agricultural Universities, Extension Centres, Krishi Vigyan Kendras etc. in many states, absence of proper harvesting technologies and cold storage facilities for the produce, absence of highly scientific farm marketing systems, encouragement for allied activities like horticulture, floriculture etc. At least a portion of our poor farmers' burden is reduced by the fertilizer subsidy scheme of the Government. But we have to come out of the stereotype thinking and should welcome new initiatives. One such initiative I would like to quote is that there were suggestions for promoting phosphate-rich organic manure (PROM) as a substitute for di-ammonium phosphate (DAP) in alkaline soils which may lead to saving huge subsidy of Rs.35,000 crores being spent by the government on DAP and single super phosphate (SSP) fertilizers now. Expert opinions suggest that using rock phosphate and organic manure to make PROM is quite effective and beneficial as rock phosphate is not water soluble and is retained by the soil. After use for one crop, because of its residual effect it can be used for the second crop too thereby serving two seasons and is doubly efficient. I would suggest that Government must initiate a study on this and work out the possibilities of implementing this PROM issue.

Urea play a vital role in our fertilizers component. For the Urea producing fertilizer industries using Naptha for production, the previous United Progressive Alliance (UPA) government's directive to switch over to gas to be eligible for any subsidy after June 30, 2014 has come as a heavy blow. 

In Tamil Nadu there are two major naptha-based urea fertilizer plants -SPIC at Tuticorin, and Madras fertilizers Ltd. at Manali, in Chennai, a central public sector unit (PSU). The two companies produce about one million tonne of fertilizers per year. Unfortunately these two plants have to be closed down due to wrong policy of the then Union Government. Our revered leader Dr. Amma took up this issue last year itself and urged the Central Government to provide subsidy to two naphtha-based fertilizer plants in the state till gas connectivity is provided to them for switch over. Dr. Amma also urged that till such time as the two plants are given gas on an assured basis, these units will not be able to switch over to gas-based urea production as imported gas is almost as costly as naphtha. Dr. Amma urged for a relook into the whole policy. A stop gap arrangement has been made and a time period of one hundred days has been given by the Central Government to continue to use naphtha for production.

I fervently appeal to the Government to overhaul the policy so that the naphtha based Urea producing fertilizers plants do not suffer and they get subsidy till such the Government gives them Gas on assured basis. Urgent and positive action on the part of the Union Government is the need of the hour. I urge the Union Government to take a relook at the issue and arrive at an immediate solution keeping in mind the interest of lakhs and lakhs of farmers and hundreds and hundreds of workers by permitting the naphtha-based Urea producing fertilizer plants to continue to receive the subsidy from the Centre till such time when the gas connectivity is given to them. In the same breathe, I request the Government not to close down any Public Sector Fertilizer manufacturing plant in any part of the country by citing any reason like loss-making etc. as we have not set up any new fertilizer manufacturing units during the past so many years.

Now, I come to the Department of Pharmaceuticals. The Budget Estimates for this small but important Departments is kept at Rs.259.02 crores out of which Rs.210 crores for Plan outlay and Rs.49.02 crores for non-Plan outlay. The Budget outlay for this Department need much more allocation considering the scope of this Pharmaceuticals. We all know that India exports huge Pharmaceutical products and our Pharmaceutical companies have lot of Pharma patents to our credit. Even the share prices of the Pharma companies of our country always fare well in local stock exchanges and see constant northward movement Stock Exchanges worldwide wherever they are listed. But the investment in Pharma education is paultry and it does not meet the genuine requirement of the sector. This sector offers immense scope as a career and the export potential is limitless. Reasonable allocation should be made to this Department to strengthen and widen its activities.

Unfortunately, there is a very disturbing development recently by the untimely and unwarranted decision of the National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA) coming under this Department. The Authority, with effect from April 1, 2015, has allowed the pharmaceutical companies to increase the rates of 509 essential medicines which are used to treat various ailments like diabetes, hepatitis and cancer by 3.84%. The Government, if it is really interested in the welfare of the poor people, should immediately withdraw the decision to increase the prices of the essential medicines. The cost of medical and health services has risen steeply during the past decade and the increase in prices of medicines will put to increase in recurring monthly expenditure of the common man who have to consume medicines regularly unfortunately due to health complications. I humbly submit to the Government to withdraw this decision and spare the common man of financial suffering alongwith ill-health. 

Before wrapping up, I would once again thank our revered leader Dr. Amma and the Chair for this opportunity and conclude. 

DR. A. SAMPATH (ATTINGAL): Mr. Chairman, Sir, I understand that after so many years, the discussion on Demands for Grants relating to the Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers is taking place in this august House.

Sir, this Ministry consists of three Departments. I am having the Reports of these three Departments. They are: Department of Fertilizers; Department of Chemicals and Petrochemicals; and Department of Pharmaceuticals. 

Of these three Departments, one is concerned with the agriculture; the second is more concerned with the industry; and the third is concerned with my life and the lives of others also. 

Sir, I am not going into the statistics. But anyway we were very curious to see that that the Chairman of the Standing Committee concerned himself has participated in this discussion. The Chairman who is bound to present the Report in this august House, himself has participated in the discussion. This way, my job has been curtailed, if not reduced! He has made some recommendations and comments. He has also made some criticisms. 

Sir, here, I would like to get the support of the Chair also. In the 5th Report of the Standing Committee on Chemicals and Fertilizers, Department of Fertilizers, Demands for Grants (2014-15), at page 57, para 7 says:

“REVIVAL OF CLOSED/SICK PSUS

The Committee have, time and again, emphasized the need for expeditious revival of closed/sick units of fertilizer companies, particularly, in the context of augmenting indigenous production of fertilizers and to make the country self-reliant in fertilizer sector. ”

The hon. Minister is here. I have been in constant touch with him because of the fertilizers and chemicals of Travancore from my State.

Sir, this Report further says:

“Out of nine public sector fertilizer companies under administrative control of the Department of Fertilizers, three companies, viz., Fertilizers and Chemicals (FACT), Madras Fertilizers Limited (MFL) and Brahmaputra Valley Fertilizer Corporation Limited are sick; and two companies, viz., Fertilizer Corporation of India Limited (FCIL) and Hindustan Fertilizer Corporation Limited (HFCL) are lying closed since 2002. ”

And, we are in the year 2015, now.

The same Report further says:

“Government is considering proposals for financial restructuring of three sick companies, namely, MFL, FACT and BVFCL, which inter alia  involve write off of Government of India load and the interest thereon.”

Sir, this Report contains not only comments and suggestions but also certain criticisms on the lethargic attitude of the successive Governments and the bureaucrats, who have almost destroyed the public sector undertakings in the fertilizer sector. 

Sir, I may be permitted, now, to go through the 7th Report of the Department of Chemicals and Petrochemicals, Demands for Grants (2015-16). You may know; and in this Report also, it has been mentioned regarding the sad incident, the tragic death of thousands of people due to the Bhopal Gas Tragedy.

This House also, after the commencement of the 16th Lok Sabha, has had discussion regarding the Bhopal Gas Tragedy.

Sir, with your permission, I would like to know that the Indian Council of Medical Research had discontinued all medical researches relating to the disaster way back in 1994. I would like to get an answer from the Government of India. The Monitoring Committee, set up by the Supreme Court, has been prevented from monitoring the quality of health-care provided to the gas victims at Bhopal Memorial Hospital and Research Centre (BMHRC). Why was it prevented?

With your permission, I would like to get another reply from the Government. The BMHRC does not submit periodical reports even to the Supreme Court nor does it audit its accounts through qualified auditors. Since more than Rs. 600 crore of public money is involved, I have every right to know from the Government of India as to why this has happened. 

Regarding the Department of Pharmaceuticals, our pharma industry is growing. I also take pride in that. Every year, according to the latest reports, the pharma business is around Rs. 70,000 crore. At the same time, we all know that 2.5 million children are born every year in this nation. Six types of immunity vaccinations are necessary during their childhood. But three Public Sector Undertakings which produce the vaccines are not fully operational and they are working below their capacity. My humble submission to the Government through you is that free vaccination should be provided to all the children. Why I say so is that in this House, we have discussed about the non- availability of the anti-rabies vaccines. India is a country where the largest number of people suffer with the dog-bites in the world. In this country, the largest number of people especially the children below 14 years of age, die due to rabies. But we are not getting the free vaccination. It is a very serious thing. Even in Delhi, it is happening. It is just like the farmers’ suicide. We have started the discussion at least for the farmers who have committed suicide. Just like this, because of rabies infection, the poor people are put to death. It is just like hang man’s knot. There are certain people who are crying for the rights of the animals like dogs and monkeys. But who will cry for the rights of the poor children and the poor men? One has to provide them with medicines. 

Every year, there is an increase in the prices of about 10 to 20 per cent for the life saving drugs. For a particular patient, one medicine may be an essential drug and to another person, it may not be an essential drug. 

Here, the Chairman has submitted the report in this august House. The Standing Committee on Chemicals and Fertilizers has given the recommendations that the number of the essential drugs should be increased to 500. This is number one. The second thing is that its prices should be controlled.

The third thing is that under the guise of the FDI, it should not be utilized for the purchase of swallowing of the existing medical pharma companies working in India. They should create more jobs opportunities. They should start more pharma companies and they should produce more. 

HON. CHAIRPERSON: Please conclude. 

DR. A. SAMPATH: I am going to conclude. Regarding the compulsory license under Section 3(d), there is huge pressure from various sectors and pressure groups to dilute, if not water away with the section 3(d). My humble submission is that there should not be any watering of the section 3(d). 

Last but not least, there should be High Level Committee consisting of the Parliamentarians from both the Houses. A Committee should be formed and that Committee should be entrusted with the task of reviewing the drug policy of this nation. 

Thank you. 

* SHRI P.R. SUNDARAM (NAMAKKAL) : It is an accepted fact that the fertilizers play a significant role in agriculture. But the indigenous production of fertilizers is not adequate to meet the domestic consumption and every year our country is facing fertilizers shortage which in turn affects agricultural production.

To meet domestic consumption, there is a need to develop the existing fertilizers units in the country.

Out of the 30 fertilizer firms in the country, only three units in the state of Tamil Nadu do not have linkage to gas grid. Though substantial investments have been made for conversion of plants from naphtha to natural gas, we are left with no other option but to use naptha as feedstock for production of urea and ammonia in the absence of gas connectivity.

Therefore, the Government of Tamil Nadu under the guidance of our Puratchi Thalaivi Amma has been seeking the Central Government for extension of subsidy to the naphtha based fertilizer units in the state until there was enough supply of gas to the Madras fertilizers and spic units in Chennai and Tutocorin.

While thanking the government for extending subsidy up to this month of April 2015 and further extension from 16th of this month, I also urge the government through this august House to allow the functioning of the naphtha based fertilizer plants with the subsidies continued till such gas connectivity is provided to those units in Tamil Nadu as these urea plants had suffered huge losses last year due to suspension of operation for three months between the months of September and October 2014. Besides, frequent shut down and reopening of plants resulted in additional expenditure of Rs.10-15 crore.

The government had notified the new investment policy in January 2013 mainly to facilitate fresh investment in urea sector to reduce India's import dependency in urea sector. It is informed that this policy would support revival of closed units in the country and would encourage joint venture abroad in resource rich countries.

The government has just recently announced for revival of 5 closed urea plants in the country with the objective to become self-sufficient urea production in the next five years. Even though the announcement is late after three years of the notification of New Investment Policy, I thank the government for having decided to revive the closed urea units in the country. 

As our country is producing about 22 million tonnes of urea and imports about 8-9 million tonnes to meet the shortfall, it is welcome move and the government should also give importance for speedy execution of the proposal of effective functioning of fertilizer closed urea units instead of importing huge amount of urea from foreign countries with a burden on the foreign exchange. By encouraging imports of million tonnes of urea will not achieve objective of reducing subsidies but lead to closure of existing fertilizer units. 

In this connection, I once again urge the government to take action for the speedy revival of closed fertilizer units in the country without further delay.

The government decided now to allow production 100 per cent of neem-coated urea. I hope usage of neem coated urea would increase the agricultural production with less usage of urea. However, the government should encourage the farmers by providing additional subsidy for the neem coated urea.

Because of excess use of fertilizers and pesticides the quality of the soil has been declining every year. There is no monitoring system for the periodic testing of soil condition in the country. It is the duty of the government to set up soil testing centres at the block level especially to monitor the residue level of fertilizers and pesticides.

I am also concerned about the diversion and smuggling of urea to non agricultural purposes. Nearly 10 to 15% of urea has been diverted for the non agricultural purposes and being smuggled to neighbouring countries. Therefore, I request the government to establish institutional mechanism in cooperation with the state governments to take notice of instances of divergence of fertilizers across the border.

On behalf of my party All India Anna Dravida Munnetra Kzhagam and under the dynamic guidance of our hon. Puratchi Thalavi Amma, I feel it is my duty to list out again some of my suggestions and recommendations to the notice of the Government through this Demands on Grants for the year 2015-16 for the benefit of farmers and agricultural sector.

There is a need to provide continuous subsidy and support to the napthabased fertilizer plants until equipped with gas grid.

The government should take action to minimise import of fertilizers.

The government should also encourage neem coated fertilizers by providing incentive to the farmers.

The government should take stringent actions on the divergence of fertilizers for non agricultural purpose and should immediately prevent smuggling of fertilizers to foreign countries.

The government should also support the state governments in setting up of soil testing centres at block level mainly to undertake periodical inspection on the residue level of fertilizers and pesticides.

I hope that the hon. Minister would take into consideration all my suggestions and take appropriate action as soon as possible. 

*श्रीमती रेखा वर्मा (धौरहरा)ः माहवार एवं राज्यवार अनुमान के आधार पर उर्वरक विभाग मासिक आपूर्ति योजना जारी करके राज्यों को पर्याप्त मात्रा में उर्वरकों का आवंटन करके तथा एक ऑनलाइन वेब आधारित निगरानी प्रणाली जिसे उर्वरक निगरानी प्रणाली भी कहा जाता है। राज्य संस्थानिक एजेंसियों जैसे मार्कफेड आदि के माध्यम से रेलवे रैक के इंडेंट देकर आपूर्तियों को कारगर बनाया है। उर्वरक पोषित करने के लिए सुधारात्मक कदम उठाये जाते हैं। एफ.सी.ओ. राज्य सरकारों को तर्कसंगत कीमतों पर अपने-अपने राज्यों में उर्वरक उपलब्ध कराने के लिए उपयुव्त कदम उठाने की शव्ति प्रदान करता है।

उर्वरक की समय पर उपलब्धता के लिए सीतापुर की बजाय जनपद लखीमपुर के मैगलगंज में उतारा जाये, जिससे समय पर खाद उपलब्ध होने का प्रभाव उत्पादन पर व किसान की आमदनी पर पड़ेगा। कीटनाशक रसायनों की गुणवत्ता में सुधार की आवश्यकता है तथा उर्वरक सब्सिडी का सीधा लाभ किसानों को प्रत्यक्ष हस्तांतरण द्वारा देने की व्यवस्था की जाये। इन प्रयत्नों से किसानों को सीधा लाभ प्राप्त होगा, जिससे उनकी आमदनी बढ़ेगी।

SHRI VARAPRASAD RAO VELAGAPALLI (TIRUPATI): I thank the Chair for giving me this opportunity.

We are all fully aware that mainly because of fertilizers, we have wonderful green revolution, and thereby India has become self-sufficient in food grains. We all know that fertilizers will boost the production by 50 per cent. Since our country is mostly agrarian, there is a greater need for larger investment in fertilizer industry. Since 1990, the fertilizer industry is in doldrums for lack of a pragmatic Government policy. There is a huge gap between demand and supply of fertilizers. A huge gap is there. 

The main three important fertilizers are urea, diammonium phosphate and muriate of phosphate. Unfortunately we are importing majority of them. Although we have been developing when compared to all other countries, unfortunately, still a majority of them is being imported. For example, we are importing 100 per cent muriate of phosphate and 70 per cent of diammonium phosphate. We are importing even urea as much as 80 lakh tonnes. It is quite unfortunate. The hon. Minister may kindly have a roadmap to come to self-sufficiency.

Coming to urea, India is using mostly urea-oriented fertilizers, thanks to the subsidy that the Government is giving. But the unfortunate aspect of that is that the subsidy on urea is resulting in a huge demand, black market, shortage and there is a big queue in the shops. Also, because of the excessive use of urea, the fertility of soil is also gradually depleting. Therefore, it is the need of the hour to re-look at the issue of subsidy on urea. I do not mean that the subsidy should be reduced. The subsidy that we give approximately to the tune of Rs.72,000 crore could be spread to the other fertilizers as well. Hence, slowly deregulation of urea will greatly help in several ways to the agrarian society. 

16.02 hrs (Dr. P. Venugopal in the Chair)

Organic fertilizer is also extremely important because we are totally using chemical fertilizers. For example, neem-coated urea is increasing the production by 10 per cent. Therefore, the Government may consider improving the organic fertilizers rather than exclusively using 100 per cent chemical fertilizers.

Now, I come to the challenges that we have before the Government. Sir, with the permission of the Chair, I have a small submission to the hon. Minister. I would like to mention here that 20 years back in Andhra Pradesh, in the Nellore district where my floor leader Mr. Raja Mohan Reddy hails from and five-time MP, 2000 acres of land had been acquired for setting up of an urea plant. Unfortunately, after 20 years and after acquiring 2000 acres of land, this has not been realized for the simple reason that there is shortage of gas. Therefore, the hon. Minister, who is always kind, young and dynamic, should re-look at that urea plant in Nellore district.

The challenges are that we need steady supply of gas to be properly ensured. Steady supply of gas is required. New units also should be started because we have been talking about ‘Make in India’ and all that. So, the focus could be that fertilizers should be produced in India. As the earlier speakers have mentioned, already we have so many companies which are now closed or running on losses or are not able to produce. If a proper attention is given, I am sure that the production of fertilizers in India could be improved.

We all know that day by day agriculture is becoming very uneconomic for the farmers and that is the reason why many of the farmers are committing suicide and it is becoming an unending saga. Therefore, the main reason for this is that if we want to improve it, the supply of fertilizers should be streamlined and the Minimum Support Price should also be raised to equate with the cost of this, plus some profit also should be given to the farmers.

I am very happy to quote what the hon. Minister has said. He said that in five to six years India will attain self-sufficiency in fertilizer. He also mentioned that in 10 years, India will become the fertilizer exporter. Therefore, we are very happy that a seasoned politician like Shri Ananthkumar is at the helm of affairs. If you have a proper roadmap, it will tremendously help the agrarian sector and also help in creation of employment. 

In this regard, I would like to mention that we have restricted the Direct Benefit Transfer Scheme only to two items – LPG and the scholarships. If the Direct Benefit Transfer Scheme is also extended to fertilizer subsidy, it will greatly help the farmers. So, I request that the Direct Benefit Transfer Scheme should also be extended to the fertilizer subsidy. 

Sir, I also have a few suggestions in this regard. Improvement in fertility of soil is very important. Soil health management should be improved. Soil testing laboratories should be established and the soil health card should also be provided to each farmer, however small he may be. 

In respect of chemicals, I would mention that very little has been offered in the Budget for chemical industries. The Excise Duty on pesticides may also be brought down on par with fertilizers. At present, it is 12 per cent. If it is brought down to 8 per cent, it will also help. The Government should also establish technology upgradation and innovation fund for upgrading technology in chemical industry. It is extremely needed there because all other fields like IT and others are getting filled up. What is now open for the end people is the chemical and pharmaceutical industry. Therefore, we need to have a roadmap in support of that. Chemical clusters on par with the plastic clusters should also be developed in India.

The Government of India has permitted to set up a petro-chemical investment region in Andhra Pradesh, starting from Vizag to Kakinada. But the amount of Rs.1200 crore, which the Government of India is supposed to give for infrastructure development, is inadequate and has not been flown to Andhra Pradesh. If that money is given, the infrastructure, which is meant for investment region, could also be developed quickly. Since many people are not coming forward, the viability gap funding system should also be adopted along with the PPP model here. 

In respect of chemicals, I have only two-three points to mention. What is required here is incentive for research and development. Pharmaceutical, as my earlier speakers mentioned, is a life saving issue. Therefore, the Government requires to promote research and development and to establish national institutes for pharma education. 

One more point that I would like to mention is that just as the education cess is available, we need to have a health cess as well so that important drugs for cancer and other diseases could also be provided at concessional rates.

The last point, which I would like to mention is that, presently a very few drugs are coming under Drug Price Controller Order (DPCO). If important drugs, particularly for cancer and other chronic diseases, are added to this, the poor and the middle class people could also be benefitted. 

Thank you very much for giving me this opportunity.

*SHRI T.G. VENKATESH BABU (CHENNAI NORTH):, I would like to express my views on the Demands for Grants for the Ministry of Chemical and Fertilizers for the year 2015-16.

The grants for the Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers go to the three Departments of the Ministry, viz. the Department of Chemical and Pretochemicals, the Department of Fertilizers and the Department of Pharmaceuticals. 

The Budget Estimates for the Department of Chemicals and Petrochemicals is pegged at Rs. 255.18 crores out of which Rs. 188 crores for Plan outlay and Rs. 67.18 crores for Non-Plan outlay. The total Estimates for this Department is almost only one fourth of total Actuals of Rs. 1208.58 crores for the year 2013-14. The huge reduction in the Budget allocation from the Actuals of the year 2013-14 done in the fiscal 2014-15 by the previous Government is being followed by this Government in the present fiscal 2015-16 also. Suffice it, to say that traversing the trodden path of the erring predecessor. 

In the Chemical Sector, there is scope for development of new and commercially producible and easily usable, bio-degradable and environment-friendly organic products by the Government owned PSU Hindustan Organic Chemical Limited (HOCL). But there is no new investment in this area and to simply to say that he HOCL is being run just for the sake of running it. It is pathetic that we as a big nation do not invest in environment-friendly technologies and produce indigenous products for our people in general and for our farmers in particular. The year after year, Government after Government, consistent reduction in Plan outlay for this Department has happened at time when there is lot of noise about unveiling of new chemicals and petrochemicals policy etc. 

Other than Chemical sector, the Government also must not fail to consider the importance attached to the Petrochemicals industries because of their vast potential for wide use of Petrochemical products and also huge employment opportunities that can be created by the industry. Leaving of this, Petrochemicals sector is completely at the mercy of the private players without any new Government investment in this sector is not a good news for a growth-hungry nation like us. I hope the Government will look into this issue with due diligence and come out with increased allocation. 

Coming to the Department of Fertilizers, the Budget Estimates for this Vital Department is slated to be Rs. 73,047.90 crores out of which Rs. 50 crores for Plan outlay and Rs. 72,997.80 crores for Non-Plan outlay. The total Budget Estimates for this Department shows no major increase in quantum despite our declared intention to help our farmers to produce more. We are aware that the huge Non-Plan outlay for this Department is to meet the fertilizer subsidy. Almost same allocation without any substantial increase from the previous year's figures means, there is no substantial increased benefit proposed to be given the end users. i.e. the poor farmers of this country. There can not be any second opinion to subsidize the input cost for our farmers in which fertilizers play major role. Our poor farmers are suffering due to various ills like economically unviable small land holdings, absence of well-planned and well-executed agricultural financing, unpredictable monsoon even though due to global climate change patterns and global environmental degradation, lack of availability of latest irrigation and farm technologies, absence of localized and area-specific farm technique teaching by the Agricultural Universities, Extension Centres, Krishi Vigyan Kendras etc. in many states, absence of proper harvesting technologies and cold storage facilities for the produce, absence of highly scientific farm marketing systems, encouragement for allied activities like horticulture, floriculture etc. At least a part of our poor farmers' burden is reduced by the fertilizer subsidy scheme of the Government. But we have to come out of the stereotype thinking and should welcome new initiatives. One such initiative I would like to quote is that there were suggestions for promoting phosphate-rich organic manure (PROM) as a substitute for di-ammonium phosphate (DAP) in alkaline soils which may lead to saving huge subsidy of Rs. 35,000 crores being spent by the Government on DAP and single super phosphate (SSP) fertilizers now. Expert opinion suggest that using rock phosphate and organic manure to make PROM is quite effective and beneficial as rock phosphate is not water soluble and retained by the soil. After use for one crop, because of its residual effect it can be used for the second crop too thereby serving two seasons and doubly efficient. I would suggest that Government must initiate a study on this and work out the possibilities of implementing this PROM issue. 

Urea play a vital role in our fertilizers component. For this Urea producing fertilizer industries using Naphtha for production, the previous United Progressive Alliance (UPA) Government's directive to switch over to gas to be eligible for any subsidy after June 30, 2014 has come as a heavy blow. 

In Tamil Nadu there are two major naphtha-based urea fertilizer plants - SPIC at Tuticorin, and Madras Fertilizers Ltd. At Manali, in Chennai, a central public sector unit (PSU). The two companies produce about one million tonne of fertilizers per year. Unfortunately these two plants have to be closed down due to the wrong policy of the then Union Government. Our reserved leader Dr. Amma took up this issue last year itself and urged and central government to provide subsidy to two naphtha-based fertilizer plants in this State till gas connectivity is provided to them for Switch over. Dr. Amma also urged that till such time as the two plants are given gas on an assured basis, these units will not be able to switch over to gas-based urea production as imported gas is almost as costly as naphtha. Dr. Amma urged for a relook into the whole policy. A stop gap arrangement has been made a time period of one hundred days has been given by the Central Government to continue naphtha for production.

I fervently appeal to the Government to overhaul the policy so that the naphtha based Urea producing fertilizers plants do not suffer and they get subsidy till such the Government gives them gas on assured basis. Urgent and positive action on the part of the Union Government is the need of the hour. I urge the Union Government to take a relook at the issue and arrive at an immediate solution keeping in mind the interest of lakhs of farmers and hundreds of workers by permitting the naphtha-based Urea producing fertilizer plants to continue to receive the subsidy from the Centre till such time when the gas connectivity is given to them. In the same breathe, I request the Government not to close down any Public Sector Fertilizer manufacturing plant in any part of the country by citing any reason like loss-making etc. as we have not set up any fertilizer manufacturing units during the past so many years. 

Now, I come to the Department of Pharmaceuticals. The Budget Estimates for this small but important Department is kept at Rs. 259.02 crores out of which Rs. 210 crores for Plan outlay and Rs. 49.02 crores for Non-Plan outlay. The budget outlay for this Department need much more allocation considering the scope of the Pharmaceuticals. We all know that India exports huge Pharmaceutical products and our Pharmaceutical companies have lot of Pharma patents to our credit. Even the share prices of the Pharma companies of our country always fare well in local Stock Exchanges and see constant northward movement Stock Exchanges Worldwide wherever they are listed. But the investment in Pharma education is paltry and it does not meet the genuine requirement of the sector. This Sector offers immense scope as a career and export potential is limitless. Reasonable allocation should be made to this Department to strengthen and widen its activities. 

Unfortunately, there is a very disturbing development recently by the ultimately and unwarranted decision of the National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA) coming under this Department. The Authority, with effect from April 1, 2015, has allowed the pharmaceutical companies to increase the rates of 509 essential medicines which are used to treat various ailment like diabetes, hepatitis and cancer by 3.84 %. The Government, if it is really interested in the welfare of the poor people, should immediately withdraw the decision to increase the prices of essential medicines. The cost of medical and health services has risen steeply during the past decade and the increase in prices of medicines will put to increase in recurring monthly expenditure of the common man who have to consume medicines regularly unfortunately due to health complications. I humbly submit my prayer to the Government to withdraw this decision and spare the common man of financial suffering along ill-health. 

Before winding up, I would like to once again thank our revered leader Dr. Amma and the Chair for this opportunity and conclude. 

Thanking you. 

*KUMARI SHOBHA KARANDLAJE (UDUPI CHIKMAGALUR): Over the years, India has developed a strong capability in producing generic medicines in almost all the therapeutic categories. These medicines are being sold mostly as branded medicines which push up the retail price of these medicines. There is still a large population of poor people in the country which finds it difficult to afford these medicines. In fact, access to quality health care is a challenge in developing country like India. According to NSSO estimates, upto 79% cost of health care in rural areas is due to cost of medicines. With 65% of India's population not having access to modern health care (WHO estimates 2008) the entire problem is compounded several times. 

The aim of Jan Aushadhi Campaign is to make available quality medicines at affordable prices for all, especially the poor and the disadvantaged. Under this campaign, less priced quality unbranded generic medicines will be made available through Jan Aushadhi Stores which inherently are less priced but are of same equivalent quality, efficacy and safety as compared to branded generic medicines.

Government is planning to procure medicines is bulk from public as well as private drug manufacturing firms and rebrand them under 'Jan Aushadhi'. These will be sold in the retail market at a competitive price, allowing consumers to buy cheaper yet quality product from the Government, Government is also planning to relaunch the "Jan Aushadhi" Campaign in a new avatar in Six States, including Karnataka from June 21, 2015 to provide cheap generic drugs to patients in Government hospitals. I welcome these decisions. 

The Department of Fertilizers is responsible for adequate and timely supply of fertilizers at affordable price in the country. Presently India is 3rd largest fertilizer producer in the world with installed capacity of 127.67 lakh MT of nitrogen and 62.08 lakh MT of phosphatic nutrient during the year 2013-14. However, the indigenous production of fertilizers has not increased to meet the growing requirement largely due to raw materials/inputs limitation and partially due to lack of new investments in urea sector in the last decade. India is completely deficient in potassic resources and has to entirely depend upon import for meeting the requirement of potash for the Indian agriculture. The country is also deficient in phosphatic resources with more than 90% requirement of the country being met through direct import of finished phosphatic fertilizers or phosphatic raw materials/intermediates for direct import of finished phosphatic fertilizers of phosphatic raw materials/ intermediates for indigenous production of phosphatic fertilizers. At present, there are 30 urea units in our country. Out of these, 27 urea units use Natural Gas (using either domestic gas/LNG or both) as feedstock and fuel and the remaining three urea units use Naphtha as feedstock and fuel. Three Naphtha units are in process for conversion from Naphtha to Gas feedstock. Availability of gas is one of the major limiting factor to the growth of urea industry in the country. The Department should play a proactive role and take up the matter vigorously with the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas ensuring that adequate quantity of natural gas is supplied without any hindrance to all the existing gas based urea units. The Department should also impress upon the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas to work out a pricing mechanism for Naphtha/FO/LSHS based units so that non-gas based units could become cost efficient. 

It is a matter of concern that the imbalance use of fertilizers has resulted in deterioration of the soil health leading to decline in the agricultural productivity. I hope that the new scheme of 'Soil Health Card' would help the farmers to check the deteriorating soil health and take corrective actions and thereby boosting the agricultural productivity in the country. It would be absolutely essential if Soil Health Card is made mandatory for purchase of fertilizers by the farmers so that they could get appropriate doses of nutrients which is balanced and essential for health and soil. I also urge that the Department in consultation with Department of Agriculture and Cooperation(DAC) and other stakeholders should make an Action Plan on the subject and before making soil health card as essential, an extensive and vigorous awareness campaign amongst the farmers may be made by the Department, DAC and all fertilizer companies about Soil Health Cards as well as regarding the ill effects of over doses of fertilizers and the benefits of balanced use of fertilizers by the farmers. 

Development of buffer godowns at nodal rake points will become a critical part of the fertiliser logistics. There are number of full and half rake points in Karnataka, where fertilizer rakes are unloaded and material is dispatched to warehouses or to consumption areas by road. Some of the inaccessible areas having less transport infrastructure will suffer shortages in supply of fertilizer. At present, there are several areas which do not have full or half rake points in Karnataka, such as CHIKMAGALUR DISTRICT, my constituency. Chikmagalur district is deprived of their due share of fertilizer supply and farmers have to pay higher cost for fertilizer, due to transportation by road. I request the Hon'ble Minister to prevail upon the Railway Ministry to consider constructing a rake point (full rake goods shed or half rake goods shed) at Chikmagalur Railway Station at the earliest. 

The Indian pharmaceutical retail market, pegged at Rs. 87,000 crore annually, is dominated by branded generic products, unlike developed markets like the US and Europe. In other words, while there are very few patented medicines sold in India, most of the medicines available in the market are branded products sold by private firms. 

Department of Pharmaceuticals has 5 running PSUs under its administrative control viz. Karnataka Antibiotic and Pharmaceuticals Limited (KAPL), Rajasthan Drugs and Pharmaceuticals Limited (RDPL), Bengal Chemicals and 54 Pharmaceuticals Limited (BCPL), Hindustan Antibiotic Limited (HAL) and Indian Drugs and Pharmaceuticals Limited (IDPL). Out of these KAPL and RDPL are profit making and BCPL, HAL and IDPL are BIFR referred PSUs. Government should formulate a well thought policy without further delay to create capacity of bold drugs in the country and to attain self-reliance in bulk drugs for which revival of sick units would be extremely essential. The Department should make vigorous efforts in coordination with all concerned to revive these sick units within a fixed time line. My considered view is that the revival of these units is absolutely essential for the country to ensure availability and adequate quantity of drugs at an affordable price to the public. 

Import of major chemicals and petrochemicals has been continuously increasing at the rate of 20% from 2009-2013 due to gap between production and consumption in the country. Chemicals and Petrochemicals sector is a major segment of manufacturing industry and plays a pivotal role in various downstream industries and therefore, the Government should map out strategies for the growth of this sector reducing thereby the country's dependence upon foreign imports of chemicals and petrochemicals, boosting employment and reduction in expenditure of valuable foreign exchange. Therefore, I suggest that the Department should concerted and coordinated efforts to expedite the process of consultation with all concerned with a view to set Reverse SEZs safeguarding the interests of Indian workers and investments in these countries. I also urge that the Department should formulate an Action Plan to produce specially chemicals. With these words, I conclude. Thank you. 

*SHRI SHIVKUMAR UDASI (HAVERI): The annual turnover of the Indian Pharmaceutical Industry is estimated to be about Rs. 128044.29 during the year 2013-14. This segment of Industry has shown tremendous progress in terms of infrastructure development, technology base and wide range of products. The industry has developed excellent GMP (Good Manufacturing Practices).The Indian Pharmaceutical companies maintain highest standards in Purity, Stability and International Safety, Health and Environment (SHE) protection in production and supply of bulk drugs. The country is almost self-sufficient in case of formulations. Concern reason is that a large sum of money is being spent on import. During the year 2013-14, Rs. 17944.05 crore was spent to import medicinal and pharmaceutical product. The imports are being made on quality and economic considerations and not necessarily due to non-availability from domestic sources. I urge the Ministry that to realize the dream of 'Make in India' concept in pharmaceutical sector, the Government should boost and incentivize domestic bulk industry and discourage Indian pharmaceutical firms from importing. It is also essential that revival of closed/stick public sector units may be expedited to crate capacity of bulk drugs in the country itself and to the make the country self-reliant in bulk drugs. 

The Outlay of Rs. 12341.89 crore was proposed by the Department for the 12th Five Year Plan covering various Schemes to the Planning Commission, against which an allocation of Rs. 2968 crore was approved. However, the first three year of the 12th Five Year Plan, against a proposed outlay of Rs. 2566.86 sought by the Department, the Planning Commission allocated a Plan provision of Rs. 583 crore only i.e. Rs. 188 crore each for 2012-13 and 2013-14, and Rs. 207 crore for 2014-15. The balance outlay available for this Department, out of the total approved 12th Plan outlay of Rs. 2968 core, is Rs. 2385 crore. According to the Department, the allocation made to them falls far short of the urgent funds requirements projected by them for carrying out its laid down mandate and its vision for development of Indian Pharmaceuticals Industry under "Make in India" initiative to make India a largest global provider of quality medicines. 

National Institute of Pharmaceuticals Education and Research (NIPER) was declared as an "Institute of National importance" under the Act of Parliament on 26th June 1998. NIPER is a member of Association of Indian Universities. In addition to NIPER, SAS Nagar, Mohali the Government had set up six new NIPERs at Hyderabad, Hajipur, Ahmedabad, Rae Baeli, Guwahati and Kolkata. These New NIPERs will cater to the growing demand of the pharmaceutical sector with increased focus on R&D, particularly after the amendment of Indian Patent Act. The funds allocated to NIPER will be insufficient if NIPER buildings are to be completed in two years. The Department has not been able to spend the plan outlay allocated to them over a period of time and the actual utilization of funds by the Department had remained unsatisfactory.

The function of National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA), inter-alia include fixation and revision of prices of scheduled drug under the Drugs (Prices Control) Order (DPCO), as well as monitoring and enforcement of prices. NPPA also provides inputs to Government for policy formulation on other specific issues concerning making available affordable medicines to the consumers. All the medicines are essential and is taken when it is needed by the patient. All these medicines including Life Saving Drugs should be available in the market at affordable cost. The scope of price control needs to be enlarged to make all the drugs available especially Life Saving Drugs in all parts of the country. 

Under the strategic action plan 2015, a pilot initiative will be launched during 2015-16 to reach out all sections of society with results and will be expanded across the country in the coming 3 years covering all therapeutic groups. The Jan Aushadhi Scheme, the said Scheme will be launched in a new format from June 21st onwards in six States in the first phase. Rest of the states would be covered in second and third phases. Over a period of another one year time, Jan Aushadhi stores are expected to be opened throughout the country in the medical colleges and district hospitals in the first phase. 

More suppliers of medicines are being roped in from other Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs) as well as private manufacturers. Procurement of drugs from private manufacturers is also necessitated by the fact that CPSUs have in house capacity to manufacture only 138 products. An IT based Management Information System is to be used to ascertain availability of medicines in stores on a real time basis, accordingly trigger supply of medicines through a transparent procurement process and supply chain, patterned almost on the model of Tamil Nadu Medical Services Corporation (TNMSC). 

Out of the proposed list of 361 medicines, MRPs for 138 medicines manufactured and supplied by CPSUs, have already been fixed in consultation with NPPA. In respect of medicines procured from private manufactures or other PSUs, MRP will be fixed on the basis of rates arrived through tender process plus trade margins and other incidental costs (including excise duty, if any, and VAT component). Beyond the 12th plan period, and additional margin not exceeding 2% will also be collected to meet administrative expenses of BPPI. As BPPI has to be run on 'no profit no loss' basis the exact percentage would be worked out based on the volume of turnover at that time.

Karnataka Antibiotic and Pharmaceuticals Limited (KAPL)is a profit making joint sector company incorporated in the year 1981 (with 59% shares by the Government of India and 41% shares by Government of Karnataka through KSIIDC) The basic objective of the company was to make available life saving drugs of good quality of Karnataka Government hospitals and other institutions. The Company has been manufacturing facilities for dry power injectables, tablets, capsules, dry syrups and suspensions. The paid-up share capital of the company as on date is Rs. 13.49 crores. 

Hindustan Antibiotic Limited(HAL) is wholly owned Government company engaged in the Manufacturing and Marketing of Life Saving Drugs. HAL was established in 1954 with WHO/UNICEF assistance. HAL is the first to manufacture the Antibiotics like bulk drugs Penicillin, Streptomycin and Gentamycin. HAL has rare distinction of inventing two new molecules viz Hamycin and Aureofungin. HAL has been instrumental in ensuring the availability of life saving drugs at affordable prices in the country.

I wish that the budgetary allocation of Ministry of Chemical and Fertilizers should be increased. 

SHRIMATI SUPRIYA SULE (BARAMATI): Sir, I stand here on behalf of my party to speak on the Demands for grants of Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers. Sir, it has become a very routine thing – every time we stand on behalf of our various parties, the first line most of us speak is the cut, which every Department has unfortunately had. This is one of the most important Departments that Government of India represents. 

Sir, there are three short points that I would like to make to the hon. Minister. Shri Adsul ji, who happens to be the Chairman of the Committee, has extensively told us of the shortcomings and challenges of the Government. So, I would not bring them up.
